# Vendored crates

`parser/` and `csgoproto/` are copied from [LaihoE/demoparser](https://github.com/LaihoE/demoparser) at commit `45ca85aeac8fb0de9d385124d2c7fe0e7b8ff0c8` (`src/parser`, `src/csgoproto`), without `csgoproto/GameTracking-CS2/`, `csgoproto/update_protos.py`, the per-crate `Cargo.lock` files (the workspace lockfile at `server/Cargo.lock` governs, seeded from upstream's `parser/Cargo.lock`) and the bundled `parser/test_demo.dem` (kept locally for upstream's tests but gitignored). The changes make the build hermetic: upstream's `csgoproto/build.rs` `git clone`s GameTracking-CS2 at build time and regenerates `protobuf.rs` with protoc, and `parser/build.rs` spawns a nested `cargo run` in `../csgoproto` (which deadlocks on a shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`), so both build scripts are now `fn main() {}` and the committed, generated `csgoproto/src/protobuf.rs` is the source of truth; `prost-build` was dropped from `csgoproto`'s `[build-dependencies]`, and `parser`'s `[profile.*]` sections (ignored inside a workspace) moved to the workspace root as `[profile.dev.package.parser] overflow-checks = false`. To update, re-copy from a newer upstream commit and re-apply these changes, including the source patches below.

Upstream is MIT-licensed. Its `LICENSE` at that commit is [`LICENSE-demoparser`](LICENSE-demoparser), copied verbatim (the copyright line is upstream's, left as its template's `[year] [fullname]`); it covers both crates.

## Source patches

Each patched spot carries a `demoviewer patch` comment. They stop a crafted demo from making the parser allocate gigabytes it never fills. A failed allocation aborts the process, and `catch_unwind` cannot catch an abort:

- `parser/src/first_pass/parser.rs`: `checked_decompress_len` refuses a snappy frame that claims more than `MAX_DECOMPRESSED_FRAME` (64 MiB) once decompressed, or more than `MAX_SNAPPY_RATIO` (32) times its own size. Snappy cannot expand data more than about 21 times. Both passes' `decompress_if_needed` call it before `resize_if_needed`. Upstream sized the buffer from the header alone, so a 26-byte frame claiming `u32::MAX` bytes made every parser thread allocate and zero 4 GiB. Real CS2 frames stay under 3 MiB.
- `parser/src/first_pass/read_bits.rs`: `Bitreader::ensure_bytes_left` (with `bytes_remaining`) fails when a length read from the bit stream is longer than the bytes left. `read_n_bytes` now calls it before `vec![0; n]`, and that covers signon packets, send tables, string tables and the field decoder.
- `parser/src/second_pass/parser.rs`: `parse_packet_from_bitreader` calls `ensure_bytes_left` on each net message's size varint before `buf.resize(size)`.

These patches are the first defence. The server also parses each demo in a child process with capped memory (`crates/server/src/worker.rs`), so an allocation these patches miss costs one job, not the server.

One patch adds a feature rather than a guard: the world-entity hook behind the replay pack's doors, breakables and items on the ground (`ENT1`, `GND1`). It is off unless `ParserInputs::parse_world_entities` is set, and the server sets it only on its projectiles pass:

- `parser/src/second_pass/world_entities.rs` (new): `world_kind` picks the tracked classes (any class whose name contains `Door`, `CBreakable`, weapons and grenades that can lie on the ground, `CBaseAnimGraph`), once per class id. `WorldEntities` keeps each tracked entity's cell, offset, `m_angRotation`, `m_hOwnerEntity` and `m_iItemDefinitionIndex`, matched by the last segment of the field's name once per class and field path, and records a `WorldEntityRecord` for each entity whose state changed in a tick, and for each removal. The item's display name comes from `csgoproto::maps::WEAPINDICIES` here, so the server crate needs no `csgoproto` dependency.
- `parser/src/second_pass/entities.rs`: the decode loop passes every decoded field of a tracked entity to the table, baselines included and whether or not the prop controller wants it; entity creation and the delete branch tell the table. A creation in the slot of a tracked entity also records that entity's removal: the demo reuses slots without a delete (each round's clean-up creates the map's entities in the slots of the weapons and kits left lying).
- `parser/src/second_pass/collect_data.rs`: `collect_entities` calls `collect_world_entities()` first, before its tick filter and projectile early returns. `coord_from_cell` is `pub(crate)` so the table computes positions the same way.
- `parser/src/first_pass/parser_settings.rs` (`ParserInputs.parse_world_entities` and its `FirstPassParser` copy), `parser/src/second_pass/parser_settings.rs` (the table, built in `new()`, moved out in `create_output`), `parser/src/second_pass/parser.rs` and `parser/src/parse_demo.rs` (`world_entities` in `SecondPassOutput` and `DemoOutput`, concatenated across threads in file order like `projectiles`), `parser/src/second_pass/mod.rs`, and `false` in every other `ParserInputs` literal (`entity_handle.rs`, `bin/parse_bench.rs`, `e2e_test.rs`).

One patch is a backport of an upstream fix made after the vendored commit, to be dropped when the copy is next updated past it:

- `parser/src/second_pass/decoder.rs`, `parser/src/first_pass/sendtables.rs`: upstream `4ba136aa` (#375), the `fixed8` encoder. From CS2 build 14197 (2026-11-11) the send tables give 8-bit fields (`uint8`, `int8`, 8-bit enums, and the elements of arrays and vectors of them) the encoder `fixed8`: one raw byte, where they were varints. Read as a varint, a byte of 128 or more takes the bytes after it with it and the entity stream goes out of step, which surfaced as `EntityNotFound` 0.3 s into a matchmaking demo (a chicken's `m_SerializePoseRecipeAG2Dynamic`, in every full packet); a signed field read wrong without failing (`m_iCompetitiveRankType` 11 as -6). `Fixed8Decoder`, `Fixed8SignedDecoder` and `Fixed8Unsigned64Decoder` read the byte and keep the `Variant` type the field had; a vector's length stays a varint. Upstream's unit test came with it, and `crates/server/tests/golden_dust2_fixed8.rs` parses the demo that failed.

Not patched, because it cannot be reached from the server's inputs: `second_pass/usercmd_delta.rs` `decode_repeated` resizes to a count read from the stream, but it runs only when a `usercmd`/button prop is requested (`parse_usercmd`), and the server requests none.
